{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the start domino and traced stroke 1, the top line of the fish body. That stroke carries the fall from the nose across the back toward the tail, so it is a large part of the outline the judge sees. By the push, about 108 of 111 dominoes were connected to the start, and the fish reads clearly as a fish. I also stood back up dominoes that had been knocked over along my stretch.

Execution: I took the piece I was given and worked on it steadily from the first minute. I laid the top line in repeated batches, then switched to close inspections of the nose area and my stretch of the line to check where the chain held. I restood the dominoes that needed it. In the final minutes I kept my hands off the finished fish so no one bumped the table before the push.

Collaboration: I backed the fish idea straight away and committed to my stroke so the others could build the belly and tail in parallel. I let teammates take the joints they were working on rather than crowding the same spot, which mattered because bumps happen when people work close together. I kept the mood light and confirmed readiness with the group as the push approached.

Leadership: I led by owning a critical stroke and finishing it without needing direction. I kept my hands off the build late on to protect the result, and I kept the table relaxed in the last two minutes. I estimate my share of the table's result at about 30%, mainly through the start domino and the top body line.", "my_share_percent": 30}
